raw_case_text:
During our study, no cases of malignancy nor gastrointestinal perforation were observed. Only minor effects were observed on blood cell counts over time ( Figures 2A-C ). Alterations of blood lipid profile, resulting in the initiation of statin therapy, were not observed in any subject. Moreover, no elevation of liver enzymes was seen, and no cases of herpes zoster were found. Nevertheless, two patients were affected by serious side effects (Aspergillus fumigatus infection and Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia, respectively). The first patient was a previously healthy 69-year-old man with GCA verified by TAB in 2020. One year later, before the initiation of baricitinib, he performed a chest CT which showed three pulmonary nodules. The nodules prompted a PET-CT, showing uptake of radioactive glucose considered a possible sign of malignancy. In February 2022 (1 month after the start of baricitinib), the size of the nodules had increased and begun to cavitate. Cultures from broncho-alveolar lavage at bronchoscopy showed A. fumigatus. Baricitinib was continued, and isavuconazonium was initiated, in parallel to rapidly decreasing doses of prednisolone, which led to improvement in pulmonary CT. The second patient was a 78-year-old lady with diabetes and hypertension. She had been prescribed tofacitinib for 20 months without prior episodes of infection when she was admitted to the hospital with 1 day's duration of fevers and abdominal pain. CRP was increased (120 mg/ml) and abdominal CT showed dilated bile ducts. Enterococcus faecalis grew in blood cultures. The infection was successfully treated with piperacillin/tazobactam followed by amoxicillin/clavulanic acid. Tofacitinib was reintroduced to the patient as soon as she had ended the antibiotics.
Aside from the 15 patients described above, three individuals were excluded from the case series as they did not prevail on JAKi for 6 months or had poor adherence to therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 69-year-old man on baricitinib and prednisolone for giant cell arteritis presented with enlarging, cavitating pulmonary nodules on follow-up imaging, and a 78-year-old woman on tofacitinib presented with a 1-day history of fever and abdominal pain.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In a cohort of giant cell arteritis (GCA) patients treated with JAK inhibitors, two patients developed serious infections. The first patient, a 69-year-old man with temporal artery biopsy-verified GCA diagnosed in 2020, had three pulmonary nodules noted on chest CT 1 year later (prior to starting baricitinib) that showed FDG uptake on PET-CT suspicious for malignancy; in February 2022, 1 month after starting baricitinib, the pulmonary nodules enlarged and began to cavitate. The second patient, a 78-year-old woman treated with tofacitinib for 20 months without prior infections, presented to the hospital with 1 day of fevers and abdominal pain.
subjective.past_medical_history: Patient 1: Previously healthy 69-year-old man with temporal artery biopsy-verified giant cell arteritis (2020) treated with baricitinib and prednisolone. Patient 2: 78-year-old woman with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and giant cell arteritis treated with tofacitinib for 20 months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Patient 2 reported fever and abdominal pain for 1 day; no cases of malignancy, gastrointestinal perforation, or herpes zoster were observed in the cohort.

objective.routine_investigations: In the overall study cohort, only minor effects on blood cell counts and no liver enzyme elevations or lipid alterations requiring statins were observed. In Patient 2, CRP was elevated at 120 mg/mL and blood cultures grew Enterococcus faecalis.
objective.advanced_workup: In Patient 1, baseline pre-baricitinib chest CT showed three pulmonary nodules with FDG uptake on PET-CT; repeat chest CT 1 month after starting baricitinib (February 2022) showed nodule enlargement and cavitation, and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) culture obtained via bronchoscopy grew Aspergillus fumigatus. In Patient 2, abdominal CT demonstrated dilated bile ducts.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Patient 1 was diagnosed with pulmonary Aspergillus fumigatus infection (confirmed by bronchoalveolar lavage culture) complicating baricitinib and corticosteroid therapy for giant cell arteritis; baricitinib was continued while isavuconazonium was initiated alongside rapid prednisolone tapering, resulting in chest CT improvement. Patient 2 was diagnosed with Enterococcus faecalis bacteremia and biliary tract infection (confirmed by blood culture and abdominal CT), which resolved with piperacillin/tazobactam followed by amoxicillin/clavulanic acid, allowing safe reintroduction of tofacitinib.
